messages:
maria (eng-sre): Heads-up — customer 'acme-corp' escalated: p99 spike on POST /v1/generate (text-gen route) for the last ~90m. They report timeouts (8s) and a lot of slow tails. I grabbed the metrics: baseline p95 ~230ms / p99 ~480ms; current p95 ~1.2s / p99 ~3.8s. Error rate still low (<1%) but tail latency is unacceptable. request_id examples: rid_8f3b, rid_9a1c. API key: acct-prod-xxxx. No direct prod deploys in last 2h that I can see.

jon (oncall): Looking now. Any recent routing or kernel changes? I can toggle mitigations if we need to.

maria (eng-sre): Router config change 3h ago — small tweak to 'adaptive-batching' thresholds, but that was rolled before the spike window starts. Also saw a small increase in KV eviction on cache host kv-3 around t0+15m.

sam (support): Customer timeline: started seeing problems ~202k seconds ago, roughly when they ran a heavy batch job. They mentioned they were sending many 8k-token prompts concurrently. They increased concurrency on their side to soak backlog.

lee (infra): I can check GPU queue depths and host health. Initial glance: one serving node in cluster-gamma showed CPU steal and GPU utilization spikes aligned with the window. Could be head-of-line blocking from large sequences.

maria (eng-sre): Repro steps for us to simulate and validate:
1) Use the customer's payload (they shared a redacted prompt) with long sequences (~6k tokens).
2) Fire concurrent 40 workers hitting /v1/generate with that payload for 5m.
3) Observe p95/p99 and queue depth.

Example quick repro (python):
```python
# simplified
import requests, concurrent.futures
URL = "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate"
HEADERS = {"Authorization":"Bearer acct-prod-xxxx"}
PAYLOAD = {"model":"redwood-large-2026","input":"<6k-token prompt>"}

def call():
    r = requests.post(URL, json=PAYLOAD, headers=HEADERS, timeout=10)
    return r.status_code, len(r.content)

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(40) as ex:
    futures = [ex.submit(call) for _ in range(200)]
    for f in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures):
        print(f.result())
```

jon (oncall): Nice. While we run that, we should apply immediate mitigations (playbook):
- Apply short-term per-customer concurrency cap (e.g., 10) via rate-limiter.
- Enable circuit breaker for this API key (fail fast after 2s of server-side queue delay).
- Add model fallback rule: route to redwood-medium if redwood-large queue depth > threshold.
- Warm prefix cache and enable prefix reuse for repeated prompts.

Can someone own the rate-limit change? I can do circuit breaker toggle and model fallback.

arjun (prod-eng): I can do the rate-limit via console internal API. Proposed rule:
```
POST /internal/rate_limits
{
  "scope": "api_key",
  "key": "acct-prod-xxxx",
  "concurrency_limit": 10,
  "burst": 12,
  "ttl": 3600
}
```
I'll roll that to a 5-minute preview window first.

lee (infra): I'll check node-level queues and, if needed, drain the hot node (cluster-gamma-node-07) — we can cordon it and let autoscaler rebalance. Also inspecting KV cache host kv-3.

sam (support): I informed the customer we're investigating and asked for the exact payload IDs. They're willing to accept a temporary cap if it helps.

maria (eng-sre): Running synthetic now with 40 workers — initially p99 shot to ~4.2s on our stage cluster when we use long sequences. Observed one node with very high read latencies from KV (kv-3). Kernel logs show many epoll wakeups and high CPU steal on that host.

jon (oncall): I've enabled circuit breaker with a 2.5s service-level queue threshold for this route for acct-prod-xxxx — policy id cb-2026-042. Also configured immediate 503 on breach to avoid long tails.

arjun (prod-eng): Rate-limit rule pushed as a preview (rule id rl-2026-098). It's live in canary; snapshot shows concurrency reduced to ~9 for that key. Customer is no longer able to open >12 concurrent requests.

lee (infra): Cordoned cluster-gamma-node-07 and triggered drain. Found an old kernel driver mismatch that caused CPU steal under contention — raising infra ticket INFRA-837 to patch and coordinate rolling restart.

maria (eng-sre): Added a model-fallback route in the router config: when per-shard queue_depth >= 6, route to redwood-medium via policy fallback-2026-01. This will reduce p99 at the cost of quality but keep availability. Config snippet:
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
policies:
  - condition: queue_depth >= 6
    action: fallback_model
    target: redwood-medium-quant
    reason: p99_tail_mitigation
```

sam (support): Customer accepted temporary cap + fallback. They're OK with slightly lower quality until tails are fixed.

latency-bot: Automated note — post-mitigation synthetic check started at t+25m. Baseline run shows p95=350ms p99=560ms (improved). Will post full report in 10m.

maria (eng-sre): Observed immediate improvement after CB + rate-limit + fallback: p99 decreased from 3.8s -> ~600ms on our canary traffic. Not perfect but much better. Taking next steps:
- Keep rate-limit + CB + fallback active for 1h.
- Continue draining/patching the kernel on node-07 (lee).
- Investigate KV host kv-3 evictions (maria + lee).
- Add long-seq workload to regression suite and add alert on p99 delta > 200% for that route (arjun).

arjun (prod-eng): I'll add the regression test and create an alert rule: metric route:/v1/generate p99 relative >2x baseline over 5m => paging to eng-sre.

lee (infra): Patch job scheduled and will run during the 30min maintenance window. I expect node-07 to be back in 40m.

jon (oncall): Status update for timeline: t+5m applied CB, t+7m rate-limit canary, t+12m fallback, t+25m observed improvement. I'll leave circuit-breaker in place until we finish the infra patch and confirm KV stability. Will monitor 1:1 with latency-bot.

sam (support): Customer notified and will confirm if their production load is back to normal. They appreciate the proactive fallback.

maria (eng-sre): Post-mortem actions (short list):
- Hot-path: better isolation for long-sequence requests (quota/plan changes) — product to eval.
- SLO guardrails: default per-key concurrency caps for large-token models.
- Platform: make fallback policies first-class and easily togglable per-tenant.
- Ops: add automated detection for KV host eviction correlated with latency tails.

jon (oncall): I'll convert this thread into an incident runbook card with the playbook steps and include the curl/py repro. Also adding temporary runbook entry for 'long-sequence p99' mitigations.

maria (eng-sre): Marking action items:
- arjun: add regression + alert (ETA 2d)
- lee: infra patch + node drain (ETA 40m)
- i (maria): follow up on KV cache tuning and prefix-warmup (ETA 3h)
- jon: keep CB live and monitor (ETA until cleared)
- sam: follow-up with customer and get final confirmation

jon (oncall): quick note — we should consider a platform-level circuit: an automated fallback to medium/quantized models for any key that exceeds token-concurrency threshold for >3m. I'll write a short proposal after this incident.

maria (eng-sre): Final update 40m after start: node patched and rejoined; KV evictions decreased; canary p99 steady ~520-580ms; leaving mitigations for 1h more then rolling back gradually. Closing the immediate escalation. Thanks all :clap: :thumbsup:

sam (support): Customer confirmed their observed p99 dropped too. They will reopen if they see regression. Thanks team. :heart:
